ledger.note: 20 September 1296: the partition of Saxony. The deed 'definitely partitioned Saxony, providing Saxe-Lauenburg for the brothers', with 'the Land of Ratzeburg, the Land of Darzing (later Amt Neuhaus), and the Land of Hadeln'; the lead: 'a reichsfrei duchy that existed from 1296 to 1803 and again from 1814 to 1876'.

region.text: the Land of Ratzeburg, the Land of Darzing and the Land of Hadeln

ledger.note: 23 August 1420: Perleberg. Bergedorf, the Vierlande and Geesthacht 'were to be irrevocably ceded to the cities of Hamburg and Lübeck' (Treaty of Perleberg); the Herrschaft of Bergedorf, the Vierlande, half the Saxon Wood and Geesthacht had been pawned to Lübeck in 1370. Eric V had attacked Prince-Elector Frederick I of Brandenburg in 1420.
1575: Steinhorst. 'Saxe-Lauenburg ceded the bailiwick of Steinhorst to Gottorp in 1575.'

1689: the Ascanian line ends. 'The Lauenburg line of the House of Ascania became extinct in the male line' in 1689, and the duchy 'passed to the House of Welf and its cadet branch House of Hanover'; on 9 October 1693 the Hamburg settlement left Celle 'already de facto holding most of Saxe-Lauenburg' with the duchy. Entered as a dynasty step inside one state (rule 2).
1689: Hadeln. The Land of Hadeln 'was disentangled from Saxe-Lauenburg in 1689 and administered as a separate territory under imperial custody'; it was ceded to Bremen-Verden in 1731.

1803: the page's end year (lead: 'existed from 1296 to 1803 and again from 1814 to 1876'). The page says only that 'The duchy was occupied by French troops from 1803 to 1805', that France 'ceded Saxe-Lauenburg, which it no longer held, to the Kingdom of Prussia' in December 1805, and that it was recaptured in 1806 and annexed to the First French Empire on 1 January 1811. It names no act in 1803 itself, so the end is confidence 1.

certainty.note: The page names the three lands of 1296 and the later cessions but gives no area or boundary; the circles are stand-ins.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 for batch eu-09-x (1 page; budget 1-2). New state: Cliopatria has no Saxe-Lauenburg row.

SCOPE. The page says the duchy 'existed from 1296 to 1803 and again from 1814 to 1876'. This dossier covers the first existence, to 1803, the project's era; the second (1814-76: Hanover, Prussia, Sweden, Denmark, then the Prussian district) is not entered, and the successor named is Prussia. The page's 1803 end is its lead only: nothing dated 1803 is described except the French occupation 1803-05, so the dissolve is confidence 1.

Items on the page left out of the ledger: Danish conquest 1203 and reversion to Albert I of Saxony 1227 (before the state); the election of two kings in 1314; the 1401 succession of Eric IV; the Thirty Years' War (Augustus 'always remained neutral'); the 1689-93 succession conflict between Celle and Danish Holstein (no war entry: the page names no battle); the 1731 cession of Hadeln to Bremen-Verden.
